descriptions.longDescription:
Met Open Formulieren kunnen beheerders snel slimme formulieren realiseren die  ontsloten worden middels een API. Met de Open Formulieren JavaScript `SDK`_  kunnen gepersonaliseerde formulieren opgehaald en getoond worden aan de  gebruiker, in de stijl van de gemeente. Hierbij zijn velden vooringevuld indien  mogelijk en zijn er keuzes beschikbaar afhankelijk van de gebruiker, mits deze  is geauthenticeerd.
Door gebruik te maken van een plugin-architectuur kan Open Formulieren flexibel worden ingericht met submission backends (bijv. Open Zaak), authenticatie  middelen, betaalproviders, kalender applicaties en pre-fill services.
Open Formulieren is ontwikkeld volgens de Common Ground principes, specifiek  voor gemeenten en met focus op gebruiksgemak voor zowel burger als beheerder.

Using Open Forms, administrators can quickly create powerful and smart forms that are exposed via an API. With the Open Forms JavaScript SDK, personalized forms can be retrieved and shown to the user. The form blends in with an  existing website using various styling options. Form fields are pre-filled whenever possible and personalized choices are shown depending on the user, if authenticated.
Using a plugin-based architecture, Open Forms allows for flexible submission  backends (e.g. Open Zaak), authentication schemes, payment providers, calendar apps and pre-fill services.
Open Forms is developed in line with the Common Ground principles, specificly for municipalities and with a strong focus on usability for both the civilian users and the administrator.

results.title: Project health (CHAOSS)
results.description: How active and widely carried the project is: the bus factor, the spread over organisations, how change requests and issues are handled, and how often it releases. Informative: shown, not rated.
results.message: 6 of 6 CHAOSS metrics measured. They are shown for information and do not count in any rating.

metrics.name: Contributor Absence Factor
metrics.explanation: The fewest people who together made half of the commits on the default branch in the last 12 months, of the 100 contributors GitHub reports, among 15 human contributors. At 1 the project depends on a single person. Bots are left out; one person with several accounts or addresses counts more than once.

metrics.name: Organizational Diversity
metrics.explanation: Organisations are told apart by the email domain of the latest 300 commits of the last 12 months (295 commits by people, after the .mailmap) and, for a personal or hidden address, by the company on the author's public profile. The largest is maykin.nl (2 authors), with 56% of the 262 commits whose organisation is known; 11% of the commits come from 2 of 8 authors whose organisation stays unknown. Only these counts are kept, no names, addresses or companies; an organisation is named only when several authors share it.

metrics.name: Change Request Closure Ratio
metrics.explanation: 161 change requests were closed (merged or not) and 207 opened in the last 90 days, bots included. Below 1 the open backlog grows; above 1 it shrinks.

metrics.name: Time to First Response
metrics.explanation: The median time to the first comment or review by someone other than the author, over the 15 latest change requests opened by people between 2026-08-22 and 2026-11-13. 10 got a response; 5 had none yet. Bots are left out.

metrics.name: Issue Response Time
metrics.explanation: The median time to the first comment by someone other than the author, over the 15 latest issues opened by people between 2026-08-22 and 2026-11-13. 8 got a response; 7 had none yet. Bots are left out.

metrics.name: Release Frequency
metrics.explanation: 51 final releases were published in the last 12 months, about one every 7 days, counted from the version tags. The latest final release is from 2026-10-30. Drafts and pre-releases are left out.

Only the 200 most recently updated issues of each kind were read.

Vulnerabilities are read from the published GitHub security advisories, from draft to publication. Their response time, unpublished advisories and Dependabot alerts need admin rights and are not measured.
161 of 320 issues were opened by the maintainers themselves; they have a fix term but no response term.
No issue carries a blocking label (such as blocker or critical), so every bug counts as an other bug.
